examples.title: A regular inequality join keeps every earlier price
examples.sql:
SELECT o.id, p.effective_at::VARCHAR AS price_time, p.price
FROM orders o LEFT JOIN prices p
  ON o.sku = p.sku AND o.ordered_at >= p.effective_at
WHERE o.id = 104 ORDER BY p.effective_at;

examples.title: Match the closest earlier price for each order
examples.sql:
SELECT o.id, o.sku, p.effective_at::VARCHAR AS price_time, p.price
FROM orders o
ASOF LEFT JOIN prices p
  ON o.sku = p.sku AND o.ordered_at >= p.effective_at
ORDER BY o.id;

examples.title: Calculate amounts while preserving the unpriced order
examples.sql:
SELECT o.id, o.qty, p.price, o.qty * p.price AS amount
FROM orders o
ASOF LEFT JOIN prices p
  ON o.sku = p.sku AND o.ordered_at >= p.effective_at
ORDER BY o.id;

sampleSpecs.title: The price history
sampleSpecs.description: Prices apply from their effective timestamp, including that instant, until the next price for the same SKU.

sampleSpecs.title: Orders placed along that timeline
sampleSpecs.description: Order 101 predates every WREN price. FIR has its own independent price history.

challenge.title: Find orders with no earlier price
challenge.prompt: Return id for orders with no applicable price at or before their timestamp. Keep the SKU equality condition.
challenge.hint: An equality join mistakes an unchanged price for a missing one. Use ASOF LEFT JOIN and then test the matched price ID.
challenge.starter:
SELECT o.id FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN prices p
  ON o.sku = p.sku AND o.ordered_at = p.effective_at
WHERE p.id IS NULL ORDER BY o.id;
challenge.solution:
SELECT o.id
FROM orders o
ASOF LEFT JOIN prices p
  ON o.sku = p.sku AND o.ordered_at >= p.effective_at
WHERE p.id IS NULL ORDER BY o.id;
challenge.success: Only order 101 lacks an earlier price. Orders between price updates use the previous price.
